name: Competitor Database
description: Structured database of products by industry. Records navigation, pricing, onboarding, dashboard layout, mobile experience, features, strengths, weaknesses and UX observations. Used by research agents to benchmark any new build.

items.title: QuickBooks
items.summary: The SMB accounting default. Broad features, dense dashboard, invoicing-first workflows.
items.content: QuickBooks is the incumbent SMB accounting tool. It sets the mental model for invoicing, expense tracking, and reports, but its density and upsell-heavy flows frustrate users.

metadata.dashboard_layout: Dense widgets: income, expenses, profit, bank feed
metadata.feature_set: Invoicing, expenses, payroll, inventory, tax, reports
metadata.ux_observations: Users complain about feature-discovery and confusing upsells; a simpler focused dashboard is a differentiator.

items.title: Xero
items.summary: Cleaner, simpler accounting competitor - the UX benchmark for modern SMB accounting.
items.content: Xero is the cleaner alternative: a minimal bank-feed-centric dashboard and simpler navigation. Widely seen as better designed than QuickBooks for small teams.

metadata.dashboard_layout: Minimal: bank balance, cashflow chart, pending invoices
metadata.feature_set: Invoicing, bank feeds, bills, payroll, projects
metadata.ux_observations: Proves simple dashboards beat dense ones for SMB trust and satisfaction.

items.title: Zoho Books
items.summary: Budget-friendly, deep-featured accounting with a steeper learning curve.
items.content: Zoho Books offers near-enterprise features at low cost. Value-focused but with a busier UI and steeper learning curve - targets price-sensitive SMBs.

metadata.feature_set: Invoicing, expenses, inventory, project billing, multi-currency
metadata.ux_observations: Price wins customers, UX loses some of them; opportunity for simpler mid-tier.

items.title: HubSpot
items.summary: The free-CRM wedge: easy start, generous free tier, powerful when adopted.
items.content: HubSpot converts via a genuinely useful free CRM. Its onboarding is smooth and the dashboard centers on deals pipeline with a simple record model. The catch: premium features and paid tiers are heavily marketed inside the product.

metadata.feature_set: Contacts, deals, marketing email, forms, help desk
metadata.strengths: Ease of use, free tier, ecosystem
metadata.ux_observations: The free CRM sets the bar for frictionless signup and simple pipeline UX.

items.title: Salesforce
items.summary: The enterprise standard: unmatched power, steep learning curve.
items.content: Salesforce is the enterprise incumbent. Extremely customizable but notoriously complex. Sets expectations for admin-level configuration and enterprise integrations, not for ease of use.

metadata.feature_set: Leads, opportunities, forecasting, automation, analytics, app platform
metadata.ux_observations: Demonstrates that simplicity is a real differentiator against enterprise incumbents.

items.title: Pipedrive
items.summary: Deal-first CRM; the pipeline is the entire product - the UX benchmark for pipeline simplicity.
items.content: Pipedrive is built entirely around the visual pipeline. Minimal record fields, drag-drop deals, activity-based selling. Proof that one strong metaphor beats feature sprawl.

metadata.feature_set: Deals, activities, contacts, email sync, reporting
metadata.ux_observations: A single strong interaction model (pipeline) creates a coherent, easy product.

items.title: ClickUp
items.summary: Everything-in-one PM with a huge feature set; powerful but can overwhelm.
items.content: ClickUp targets the all-in-one user with views, docs, goals, and automation. Enormous feature breadth creates discovery problems; the value is there but hidden behind complexity.

metadata.feature_set: Tasks, docs, goals, time tracking, automation, dashboards
metadata.ux_observations: Warns against feature sprawl - the all-in-one approach must manage cognitive load.

items.title: Asana
items.summary: Polished, balanced PM: strong UX, clear hierarchy, good for structured teams.
items.content: Asana is the UX benchmark among full PM tools: clean hierarchy (projects -> tasks -> subtasks), lists/timeline/boards, and a calm interface. Simpler than ClickUp, less powerful than Jira.

metadata.weaknesses: Can get expensive, fewer dev-oriented features
metadata.ux_observations: Shows hierarchy clarity and restrained feature growth create an effortless product.

items.title: Monday.com
items.summary: Visually rich work OS; color-coded boards win non-technical teams.
items.content: Monday.com's visual boards (color, groupings, automations) appeal to non-technical teams. Great for marketing/ops; can feel busy for power project managers.

metadata.ux_observations: Color-coding and friendly visuals make work software feel approachable to non-engineers.

items.title: Notion + AI
items.summary: The workspace + AI assistant model: AI inline where you already work, not a separate tool.
items.content: Notion demonstrates the winning AI UX: AI appears inline in the document where the user already works (ask, autofill, edit). This beats standalone chat tools for workflow integration.
rules: AI inline in the work surface

metadata.feature_set: Docs, databases, wikis, AI inline, sync
metadata.weaknesses: Learning curve, performance on large DBs
metadata.ux_observations: AI works best embedded in context, not as a separate product.

items.title: ChatGPT
items.summary: The general chat assistant baseline: single input, threads, shareable responses.
items.content: ChatGPT set the chat baseline. Key patterns: thread history, code blocks with copy, share links, and now agentic features. Its UX is the reference for any conversational AI product.

metadata.feature_set: Chat, file upload, image gen, code, browsing, memory
metadata.weaknesses: Hallucination risk, trust, content policy friction
metadata.ux_observations: Zero-friction onboarding (type and go) is the gold standard for AI products.

items.title: Intercom (Fin)
items.summary: Customer service AI copilot embedded in a support inbox, with agent handoff.
items.content: Intercom's Fin shows how to combine AI chat with human handoff: AI answers common issues, escalation is one click, and everything lives in the existing inbox. Smooth hybrid AI-human UX.

metadata.onboarding: Connect help content, deploy in hours
metadata.feature_set: AI answers, human handoff, help center, analytics
metadata.strengths: Fast value, hybrid model, measured resolutions
metadata.ux_observations: Clear handoff between AI and humans keeps trust while cutting ticket volume.

items.title: Shopify
items.summary: The commerce benchmark: fast setup, clean admin, and the most optimized checkout flow.
items.content: Shopify's admin and checkout set the bar: minimal clicks to product, clean order management, and a one-page checkout with express payments. Its success validates simplicity-first commerce.

metadata.feature_set: Store, products, checkout, shipping, marketing, analytics
metadata.ux_observations: The benchmark checkout: address autofill, express wallets, one page, no account required.

items.title: WooCommerce
items.summary: The flexible open-source option: total control, higher setup burden.
items.content: WooCommerce trades ease for control: free core, WordPress flexibility, plugin ecosystem - but setup, hosting, and maintenance are on the merchant.

metadata.feature_set: Store, products, payments via extensions, shipping, taxes
metadata.ux_observations: Shows the market split between managed simplicity (Shopify) and self-managed flexibility.
